summary: A Tesla Model 3 taxi in Paris suddenly accelerated and ploughed through a crowded area, killing a cyclist and injuring about 20 people. Early reports blamed sudden unintended acceleration, but Tesla said it found no technical fault and the driver was investigated.
technical_summary: A Tesla Model 3 taxi reportedly sped forward from a red light and could not brake, striking a cyclist, pedestrians and a van. Cause is disputed: officials first cited a stuck accelerator or braking issue, while Tesla's initial inquiry found no technical dysfunction and investigators are reviewing data.

summary: Dozens of women reported unwanted pregnancies while using the Natural Cycles contraceptive app, which tells users which days are safe for unprotected sex based on temperature readings. Regulators began an investigation.
technical_summary: The app uses an algorithm to predict daily fertility from basal body temperature and cycle data and labels days green or red. No method is fully reliable, and results also depend on users following instructions precisely; some users became pregnant on days marked safe.

summary: Twitter's automated moderation flagged photos and videos of rocket launches as intimate content, locking several space-news accounts out. The accounts were later unlocked.
technical_summary: Twitter's machine-learning content-moderation tools misclassified rocket images as sexual or intimate media and triggered account suspensions at a high confidence threshold. A former employee said relying less on human moderators raises the rate of incorrect censorship; the company had cut many moderation staff.

summary: An automated license plate reader in San Francisco produced a false stolen-vehicle hit, and officers stopped an innocent woman at gunpoint and held her in handcuffs for nearly 20 minutes. An appeals court reinstated her civil rights lawsuit.
technical_summary: An ALPR misread a plate and matched it to a stolen vehicle in a hot list. Officers did not visually confirm the plate before a felony stop, and the department reportedly had no formal verification policy assigning that task despite training that hits require verification.

summary: A poor-quality deepfake video of Ukrainian President Zelensky appearing to tell Ukrainians to surrender spread online and appeared in a hacked TV news ticker. It was debunked quickly and removed from major platforms.
technical_summary: Attackers produced a synthetic video of the Ukrainian president and distributed it on Ukrainian websites and social media, while a TV channel's news ticker was also hacked to show similar surrender messages. Visible artifacts and a rapid denial limited its impact.

summary: A university computer science department used a machine-learning tool called GRADE to score PhD applications, trained on past admissions decisions. Critics said it could reproduce historical bias and reduce attention to lower-scored applicants; the department stopped using it.
technical_summary: GRADE predicted the likelihood that an admissions committee would approve an applicant, using patterns from past decisions such as recommendation-letter words, GPA and institution category. Low scorers received less review. Because it learned from historical decisions, it risked encoding past bias. Humans reviewed every file, per the university.

summary: An Australian TV network aired a photo of a state lawmaker that had been altered so her outfit looked more revealing. The network blamed automation in Photoshop's generative tool and apologized.

summary: Users of the dating app Coffee Meets Bagel who chose 'no preference' on ethnicity were shown mostly matches of their own ethnicity or one group. The founder said the algorithm uses data on past behavior to maximize connection.
